page: Amazon Web Services m8g.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor architecture. The configuration includes 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. It provides 64.0 GB of total RAM, sustaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile, with no integrated local storage or dedicated graphics processing units.

Benchmark measurements highlight particularly strong memory subsystem performance. The instance registers a PassMark memory score of 3213.67 in the top 10 percent of tested servers, complemented by uncached 256 MB read bandwidth of 296.67 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 133.88 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25 percent. General compute throughput aligns with median cloud benchmarks, recording 1867.0 on single-core and 15796.0 on multi-core Geekbench suites. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark database operations both rate in the top quartile.

The primary operational tradeoff centers on reliance on network-attached storage and lower efficiency in dense compute workloads like artificial intelligence inference, where 7B model prompt processing drops to 31.24 tokens per second. However, with dedicated core allocation preventing thread contention and high memory throughput, the instance delivers solid resource density for general enterprise workloads. Suitable implementations include relational and caching databases, application middle tiers, microservices deployments, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m8g.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running on the AWS Nitro System. It provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs clocked at 2.8 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The hardware configuration features no local ephemeral storage and no GPU accelerators, using an 8 Gbps baseline network uplink. Benchmark testing demonstrates exceptional memory subsystem efficiency, achieving a PassMark memory result in the top 10 percent alongside strong uncached read and write bandwidth in the top 25 percent. Compute metrics remain squarely in the median bracket across stress-ng and Geekbench workloads. Because it provides dedicated cores without simultaneous multithreading overhead, the instance is well suited for container clusters, relational databases, backend web services, and continuous integration pipelines.
